anchors.1: Not shown: missing, wrong, or you needed the interviewer to supply it.
anchors.2: Partial: mentioned, but shallow, unjustified or only after a hint.
anchors.3: Solid: correct and reasonably complete, with minor gaps you could explain.
anchors.4: Excellent: precise and justified with numbers and trade-offs, and you raised the edge cases yourself.

system-design.label: Requirements and scoping
system-design.good: You agreed on scope, scale and quality goals before designing, and wrote them down.

system-design.label: Estimation
system-design.good: You computed only the numbers that change decisions and said what each implies.

system-design.label: API and data model
system-design.good: You defined core endpoints and chose storage from the access patterns.

system-design.label: High-level design
system-design.good: You started simple, justified every component and walked the main request end to end.

system-design.label: Deep dive
system-design.good: You went one level deeper on the hardest parts with concrete mechanisms.

system-design.label: Trade-offs
system-design.good: You named alternatives, the criterion, the cost and what would change your mind.

system-design.label: Failure and reliability
system-design.good: You asked what happens when each part fails or becomes ten times busier.

system-design.label: Communication
system-design.good: You narrated your reasoning, used the board well and adapted to hints.

low-level-design.label: Requirements and scope
low-level-design.good: You clarified use cases, actors and constraints before writing classes.

low-level-design.label: Object model
low-level-design.good: Your classes and relationships map cleanly to the domain with clear responsibilities.

low-level-design.label: Patterns and principles
low-level-design.good: You applied SOLID and a pattern only where it solved a real extension problem.

low-level-design.label: Code quality and tests
low-level-design.good: Your code is readable and you identified how to test the key behaviours.

low-level-design.label: Extensibility and concurrency
low-level-design.good: You showed how new requirements fit and handled concurrent access where relevant.

low-level-design.label: Communication
low-level-design.good: You explained design choices as you made them and responded to hints.

ai-coding.label: Problem solving
ai-coding.good: You chose the approach yourself and used the assistant for implementation.

ai-coding.label: Verification
ai-coding.good: You tested each step and caught mistakes in the assistant's output.

ai-coding.label: Code quality
ai-coding.good: You kept functions small and could explain every line you accepted.

ai-coding.label: Collaboration with the tool
ai-coding.good: You asked for small, specific pieces and knew when to type it yourself.

ai-coding.label: Communication
ai-coding.good: You narrated what you delegated, why, and what you were checking.

behavioral.label: Specificity
behavioral.good: You described a real situation with concrete details and numbers.

behavioral.label: Ownership
behavioral.good: It is clear what you personally decided and did, not just the team.

behavioral.label: Impact
behavioral.good: You ended with a measured outcome and why it mattered.

behavioral.label: Reflection
behavioral.good: You named what you would do differently and what you learned.

behavioral.label: Communication
behavioral.good: The story was clear, well structured and about 90 seconds to two minutes.
